handoff: Changes requested. Blocking F1: doctor's adopting mv (doctor.ts:462) nests the orphan inside the already-existing own machine dir, with unquoted paths, so it adopts nothing (D3/AC5). Minor: hook never binds ctx.home (AC2 passes only via the global binding), checkout.json not rewritten after adoption, weak AC2/AC4/AC5 asserts, global homes map. Layout, D2 id, D9, D10 otherwise correct.

findings.title: The printed `mv` does not adopt the orphaned machine dir
findings.detail:
D3: 'prints the `mv` that adopts it (keeping the heartbeat)'. The hint is `mv ${o.dir} ${machineDir(ctx.root)}`. Any tick or command that traces (heartbeatId -> ensureCheckoutFile, appendTrace) has already created the own machine dir, so `mv old new` with `new` an existing directory moves `old` to `new/<old-name>/`. The heartbeat is not adopted, and the next tick keeps the fresh id. The AC5 test shows it: `mine/heartbeat.json` exists before doctor runs (machine-dir.test.ts:197), so running the printed command would nest. The paths are also not shell-quoted, so a home or checkout path with spaces breaks the command.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Print a command that actually adopts: replace the current dir, e.g. `rm -rf '<mine>' && mv '<orphan>' '<mine>'` (and say to stop watch first), with both paths quoted. In the test, run the printed command in a shell and assert that the heartbeat id is the orphan's afterwards.

findings.title: hook writes its trace without binding the command's norn home
findings.detail:
hook is `repo: false` and never calls ctx.locate(), so bindNornHome never runs for it. appendTrace(root, …) then resolves the home from process.env / ~/.norn rather than ctx.home (it does pass ctx.home to loadConfig two lines up). Whenever ctx.home differs from the process env, hook facts land in a different machine dir from the one tick and doctor read. The AC2 test's '"type":"hook"' assertion only passes through the process-global `homes` binding left by earlier in-process commands, and that same string can also match hook events from before the test.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: bindNornHome(root, ctx.home) after resolving marker.repo in hook. Better still, bind in one place for repo:false commands that find a marker. In AC2, check that the trace has a hook event with session_id s1.

findings.title: checkout.json is never rewritten after an adoption
findings.detail:
ensureCheckoutFile writes the file only when it is missing. After the D3 adoption, checkout.json keeps naming the old, vanished path for good, which contradicts AC1's 'a `checkout.json` naming the checkout'.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Rewrite it when it names a different checkout (it is cheap: one read per tick), or fold it into the adoption fix for F1.

findings.title: Several AC tests are weaker than their criteria
findings.detail:
AC2: machineFilesUnder matches only some names (it misses failures.json, notices.json, pr.json, base/ and the old .agents/norn/trace/ dir itself), and `before.length > 0` proves nothing. AC4: no lease is ever read, the test only checks that the leases dir exists. AC5: the comment at line 185 promises a dir 'whose checkout still exists' but builds none, so the !existsSync branch is untested.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Assert that the worktree has no .agents/norn/trace and no norn json files; read a lease back after a tick; add an existing-path fixture to AC5.

findings.title: Process-global home binding: last bind wins, never unbound (Shotgun Surgery)
findings.detail:
`homes` is a module-level Map. bindNornHome is called in context.ts:129, view/load.ts, view/trace-view.ts and doctor.ts:98, and hook forgot it (F2). Doctor's scratch units leave one entry per run. In-process tests with different homes for one repo leak the binding between commands.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Keep the binding but drop the scratch entry in doctor's drop(), or pass the home explicitly where it is known; at least bind in one place per command kind.

findings.title: checkoutOf's walk-up can pick an enclosing repo; a submodule names .git/modules/<x> as checkout
findings.detail:
A root outside git (or a bare repo with no .git) walks up and may resolve to an unrelated enclosing repo such as a dotfiles repo in $HOME. In a submodule, the common dir is .git/modules/<x>, so checkout.json names that path rather than the checkout.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Stop at the root's own top level (the root is always a located checkout), or document the case.

findings.title: `trace_dir` field now holds the machine dir (Mysterious Name)
findings.detail:
steps.ts:22 and trace-view.ts:95: `trace_dir: string; /** absolute machine dir … */`.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Rename it to machine_dir, or leave it to slice 07 (docs) if the view shape must stay.

findings.title: scratchUnit leaks its temp dir if git init throws
findings.detail:
The mkdtemp dir is created before `git init`, outside the caller's try/finally.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Remove the dir on failure inside scratchUnit.
